open_points.subject: A07 failure-detail disclosure
open_points.text: A `failure_detail` whose class is above `open` ... is returned to an agent only as its length and that class.
open_points.question: What does the disclosed length measure: Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or UTF-8 bytes after truncation to `failure_detail_bytes_max`?
options: Unicode code points
Original UTF-8 byte length
Retained UTF-8 byte length
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the retained, bounded failure detail.

open_points.subject: A16 fixed surface
open_points.text: K-11 says the fixed surface is `inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel`, while A16 says authorization is `exactly the State 0 table of primary actions`, which also includes capture, release, rollback, propose a binding, and compose and prove a flow.
open_points.question: Are all State 0 primary actions distinct callable surface operations, or are the actions omitted from K-11 unavailable or folded into its named operations?
options: Expose every State 0 primary action separately
Treat K-11 names as categories containing the omitted actions
Expose only the literal K-11 list
open_points.default_guess: Expose every State 0 primary action as a typed operation.

open_points.subject: A16 configuration re-read parsing
open_points.text: When the configuration bytes change, the kernel `re-reads it ... and takes from it only the token list`; one of the four checks is that `the file can be read and parsed`, while `Every other field of the configuration ... applies only at a restart`.
open_points.question: On a live re-read, does `parsed` require the entire installation configuration to satisfy its schema, or only syntactically valid configuration containing a valid token-list section?
options: Validate only syntax and the token-list fields
Validate the complete installation schema but apply only tokens
Parse and ignore all non-token-field errors
open_points.default_guess: Validate syntax and the token-list fields only; retain all non-token installation facts from startup.

open_points.subject: A16 configuration re-read state
open_points.text: The kernel `compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read`; when a re-read fails, `every request is refused ... until a re-read passes`, but the text does not say whether a failed read becomes the `last read`.
open_points.question: After changed configuration bytes fail validation, what digest is remembered, and must the same unchanged invalid bytes be parsed again on every request so that a later repair is detected reliably?
options: Keep the last valid digest and retry the changed bytes every request
Remember the invalid digest but retry it every request while configuration is invalid
Remember the invalid digest and retry only after its bytes change again
open_points.default_guess: Keep the last valid digest and attempt the changed configuration again on every request.

open_points.subject: A16 request-size check
open_points.text: A request's size is `counted as the bytes of the request message as received`.
open_points.question: Which bytes count toward `surface_request_bytes_max`: the complete MCP transport frame, the JSON-RPC/MCP message encoding, or only the encoded typed-operation arguments, and how is the count obtained when the MCP library supplies an already-decoded object?
options: Complete MCP message bytes excluding transport framing
Complete transport frame bytes
Canonical re-encoding of the typed operation request
open_points.default_guess: Count the exact encoded MCP message bytes after transport framing is removed and before decoding.

open_points.subject: A17 secret-file newline and control validation
open_points.text: The credential content is `decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline` and is refused if it `holds ... a control character`.
open_points.question: Exactly which trailing sequence is removed, what happens with multiple trailing newlines, and which Unicode characters count as control characters?
options: Remove one LF only and reject all Unicode control-category characters
Remove one LF or CRLF and reject ASCII C0, DEL and C1 controls
Remove all trailing line endings and reject only HTTP-prohibited controls
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one terminal LF, also removing its preceding CR when present, then reject ASCII C0 controls, DEL and C1 controls.

open_points.subject: A17 credential value serialization
open_points.text: A secret file's content is decoded as UTF-8 and the resolved value is `added as that header` and sent `verbatim`, but values containing non-ASCII Unicode are not refused.
open_points.question: May a credential contain non-ASCII Unicode, and if so, what exact bytes are sent in the HTTP header; otherwise, which character set must validation accept?
options: Require printable ASCII
Allow HTTP field-value bytes represented by a specified single-byte mapping
Encode the Unicode value as UTF-8 header bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require printable ASCII after the optional trailing line ending is removed.

open_points.subject: A17 credential-file size
open_points.text: A credential is resolved by reading its secret file, but no maximum size or over-size outcome is stated.
open_points.question: What is the maximum credential-file/value size, and does exceeding it produce `credential_unresolved`, prevent kernel startup, or cause an internal error?
options: Add a fixed release ceiling and report `credential_unresolved` per request
Use `bounded_text_bytes_max` and report `credential_unresolved`
Permit unbounded credential files
open_points.default_guess: Apply `bounded_text_bytes_max` while resolving and report `credential_unresolved` for that service request.

open_points.subject: A17 credential-header collision startup check
open_points.text: A09 says an installation whose credential header collides with a selected instance's required header `refuses to start`, while manifest operations and instance facts are otherwise read on demand and the texts do not say what startup does when the relevant manifest record or selected instance cannot be read.
open_points.question: Must startup read every selected service's manifest instance to check credential-header collisions, and what happens if that manifest or instance is absent or invalid at startup?
options: Refuse startup unless every configured credential can be checked
Start when the manifest is unavailable and repeat the collision check before each send
Check only services whose manifests happen to be readable and otherwise rely on invocation failure
open_points.default_guess: Start without requiring service manifests, but perform the credential-header collision check as a pre-send check before every request.

open_points.subject: A13 ready-node eligibility
open_points.text: `A node is ready when every input port holds its value`, but nodes or mapped elements may already be waiting on approval, service reachability or an unknown outcome, and the next node is defined only as the smallest ready node.
open_points.question: Which nodes are scheduler candidates when their inputs are present but they are concluded, partially concluded, or waiting, so the scheduler neither repeatedly selects them nor retries waits outside the permitted request?
options: Ready also requires at least one executable, non-waiting, non-concluded element
Input-ready waiting nodes remain candidates but selecting them is a no-op
Track a separate blocked state excluded from the ready-node order
open_points.default_guess: A scheduler candidate must have all inputs and at least one element that is neither semantically concluded nor waiting; concluded and waiting elements are skipped.

open_points.subject: A13 mapped-element retries
open_points.text: A mapped node runs elements that have `no concluded record and do not wait`, and `a concluded element is never executed again`, although `service_unreachable` writes a NodeExecution and is later resent, and an `outcome_unknown` execution resolved `not_applied` is also resent as a new attempt.
open_points.question: Does `concluded record` mean any existing NodeExecution or only a NodeExecution whose combined EffectAttempt state makes the element semantically final?
options: Only semantically final elements are excluded; waiting attempts may be retried as specified
Any NodeExecution excludes normal scheduling, with resume and not-applied resend as explicit separate paths
Only `succeeded` or failed-status records count as concluded records
open_points.default_guess: Treat conclusion as the semantic result of NodeExecution plus EffectAttempt resolution; waiting outcomes remain retryable only through resume or fresh approval.

open_points.subject: A13 unknown-outcome resolution
open_points.text: Rule 5 says `service_unreachable` and `outcome_unknown` wait `until the owner's resolution makes the element count as succeeded or failed`, but A11 says resolving an unknown attempt `not_applied` makes the element wait again for fresh approval rather than succeed or fail.
open_points.question: After an unknown outcome is resolved `not_applied`, is the element waiting, succeeded, or failed for A13 readiness and run completion?
options: Waiting for fresh approval as A11 specifies
Failed
Succeeded
open_points.default_guess: It is waiting for fresh approval; the succeeded-or-failed sentence in A13 must exclude `not_applied`.

open_points.subject: A13 mapped-output materialization
open_points.text: A mapped value list is written `when the list is first delivered`, and an oversized delivered list fails the mapped node, but a mapped node can have several outputs and several outgoing edges and no order or all-before-any rule is given for measuring and delivering them.
open_points.question: In what order are mapped outputs and their fan-out edges materialized, and if one delivered list exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, may any other output already have been delivered or must all deliverable lists be checked before any delivery?
options: Validate and size every deliverable output first, then deliver all atomically
Process output ports and edges in a fixed order, preserving earlier deliveries if a later list is oversized
Fail only the oversized output while delivering the others
open_points.default_guess: Construct, validate and size all outputs that will be delivered before delivering any; if one is oversized, deliver none and fail the mapped node.

open_points.subject: A13 synthetic trace-record scheduling
open_points.text: The next executable node is selected by smallest `node_id`, while skipped and `upstream_failed` nodes write records when they become non-executable; A15 orders records that become non-executable together but does not order that group relative to still-executable ready nodes.
open_points.question: When propagation makes some nodes skipped or `upstream_failed` while other nodes are ready to execute, are all synthetic records written immediately before selecting another executable node, or are they interleaved in the global node-id schedule?
options: Write all newly determined synthetic records immediately, in A15 order
Treat synthetic conclusions as scheduler candidates ordered with executable nodes by node id
Defer synthetic records until no executable node remains
open_points.default_guess: Write all newly determined skipped and upstream-failed records immediately in A15 order before selecting the next executable node.

open_points.subject: A13 derived oversized mapped list across releases
open_points.text: An oversized mapped list fails the node but `No record of the node states that failure`; it is derived from element records and `stored_value_bytes_max` by every reader and after restart. A20 permits a new release to change ceilings and says `recorded executions are never reinterpreted`.
open_points.question: Which release's `stored_value_bytes_max` governs this durable derived conclusion after an upgrade, and how can readers preserve the original result when neither the applied ceiling nor the derived failure is recorded?
options: Pin the release or applicable ceiling in the run
Persist a record of the mapped-node size failure
Recompute under the current release, despite A20
open_points.default_guess: Pin the applicable release ceiling in the run so recovery and trace reading always derive the original conclusion.
